core_job: For people fitting things at home (DIY renovators, handypeople, tilers, renters putting up shelves): put the phone on a surface or straightedge and get the slope in the unit the job uses (%, mm/m, in/ft, 1:N, x/12 pitch, as well as degrees). It is compared against the slope the job needs and shows how much to raise which end, and the reading is filed under a job they can export. Today the app is an 11-tool grab-bag: Apple Measure's black #000000 and #FFD60A yellow look, an "iM" monogram, a converter that duplicates CalcMaster, a pedometer that duplicates MyHealth, a chat-style Quick Answers screen, and a sign-in that unlocks nothing. All of that reads as a 4.3(b) copy of Apple's built-in Measure app.
signature: Fall & Shim on the Level tab, all on the device. The live slope shows as degrees, grade %, mm/m or in/ft, 1:N and x/12 pitch at once. The user sets a target (presets shown as ratios, or anything typed such as 2%, 1:48, 1/4 in/ft, 6/12 or 1.5°) and a tolerance, and the screen shows in tolerance, too steep or too shallow, with a text label, colour and a haptic pulse. The user enters a span and gets a shim line, e.g. "Raise left end 10.5 mm". Hold and Save store the target, tolerance, span and shim in the job record. It uses the accelerometer and Set Zero already wired in level_screen.dart, with no network and no keys. The math is unit-tested: 1:12 = 4.7636° = 8.333%, 1/4 in/ft = 1.1935°, 6/12 = 26.5651°, and 1200 mm at 0.5° = 10.47 mm. Competitors not verified: WebSearch and WebFetch were blocked in this session ("Internet mode is not enabled"), so the spec bans comparative claims until someone checks competitor listings.
